//: Aim the cursor at a world point, then run a cursor-scoped console command. The most reused idiom in the tool - and 7 round-trips without a plan.
//point: x/y/z is the WORLD point. Floor cell: snap it with @map.SnapXYZ first and use aimOffsetY 0.05 - exact, three for three. Actor: pass its Pos and aimOffsetY 1.0.
//aim: Aim height is per-actor and patchy: y+0.6 missed at every horizontal offset on a Crabman where +0.4 and +0.8 both hit. SelectAtCursor takes only the NEAREST hit (TacticalView.cs:724). Probe with a cheap real command, never with `info` - info dumps all raycast hits and reports success where the cursor commands fail.
//ai: During a live AI turn the target walks away between round-trips. Set ai_enabled false first: connect var '{"name":"ai_enabled","value":"false"}'.

steps.//: The camera behaviour that owns the cursor field (CameraManager.cs:52).

FREEZE FIRST, and it is not optional: without it UpdateCursorPos (PlanarScrollCamera.cs:947,984) hands the field back to the real mouse and the identical sequence answers differently on consecutive calls. InputDisabled makes it return at :949-952. The `finally` below is what guarantees this is undone even if the plan dies here.
The aim point, computed with Unity's own operator - the plan engine has no arithmetic and does not need any.
_cursorScreenPos is private (PlanarScrollCamera.cs:157); the binder reaches it because get/set walks the declared hierarchy.
Read it back through the PUBLIC path, so the output proves where the cursor actually is rather than where it was written.
The command itself. Note `vars` returns ok:false alongside valid output; onError stays fail for everything else.

finally.//: MANDATORY. A plan that disabled input and never restored it leaves the game unusable to a human, so this runs on success, on failure, on the deadline and on cancel.
